brief: A compact desk unit with a drawer, plus a spike at a corner where three bases meet to hold a small platform.

requirements.evidence: Three full hex bases (piece:0,0,0; 1,0,0; 0,1,0) form a compact L-cluster on level 0, closed with 10 edge caps, and locked with 3 joint bolts. check_build is ok with meshClash clear. Nothing was dressed onto it as a desk; no desk props were added since the brief only named the structure.

requirements.requirement: A compact desk unit with a drawer
requirements.evidence: A notch drawer (hex-drawer-body-notch, hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf, lid, two runners) sits in the empty cell at (-1,1,0), beside the bases at (0,0,0) and (0,1,0).

requirements.requirement: A spike at a corner where three bases meet
requirements.evidence: A mount spike (spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0) sits at the junction where bases (0,0,0), (0,1,0) and (1,0,0) meet.
setSpikeAccessory platform-sm on that mount spike (spike-acc-platform-sm, qty 1). A solid spike was rejected for this, so the mount variant was used.

finish.summary: Built a three-base hex cluster with a notch drawer in the adjacent cell, a mount spike at the three-base corner carrying a small platform, closed with edge caps and joint bolts. The configurator reports no rule issues and a clear mesh check. The bill of materials is about 1479 g and 2182 min of print. Caveats: the drawer is a notch drawer rather than a free-standing one, and I did not dress the desk with props. The M6 bolts are to be hand-tightened only (about 2 N.m) for printed PETG.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
